patterns.name: Annotation-driven test injection with self-registering extensions
patterns.description: Test code declares OSGi resources (@InjectBundleContext, @InjectService) on fields or parameters. Each annotation is meta-annotated with @ExtendWith(<Extension>.class), so JUnit5 auto-registers the extension — users never write @ExtendWith unless combining behaviors explicitly.
rules: Annotation targets FIELD and PARAMETER, retention RUNTIME, @Inherited, @Documented
Meta-annotate the annotation with @ExtendWith(MatchingExtension.class)
Annotation carries configuration (filter, cardinality, timeout) as annotation members with defaults
Injected fields must not be final or private (extension enforces via disallowedFieldModifiers)

patterns.name: Generic InjectingExtension base class
patterns.description: One abstract base implements all JUnit5 lifecycle callbacks (BeforeAll/BeforeEach/ParameterResolver/AfterAll/AfterEach) and reflection plumbing once; concrete extensions supply only the annotation type, supported target types, and a resolveValue() factory.
rules: Extension extends InjectingExtension<YourAnnotation>, constructor passes annotation class + allowed target types
Override resolveValue(TargetType, annotation, ExtensionContext) as the single creation point
Static fields injected in beforeAll, instance fields in beforeEach, parameters via ParameterResolver
Honor TestInstance.Lifecycle.PER_CLASS when deciding injection timing

patterns.name: ExtensionContext.Store-scoped resources with automatic cleanup
patterns.description: OSGi resources live in the JUnit5 ExtensionContext.Store keyed per unique test id, wrapped in CloseableResource. The store closes them automatically at scope end; the BundleContext wrapper (CloseableBundleContext proxy) undoes registrations, listeners, and installed bundles left by the test.
rules: getOrComputeIfAbsent(key, factory, type) for lazy per-scope singletons
Namespace.create(ExtensionClass.class, extensionContext.getUniqueId()) — never share store slots across tests
Wrap framework objects in a dynamic proxy that records side effects and reverts them on close()
Parent-context lookup walks up ExtensionContext hierarchy for nested test classes

patterns.name: All tests run inside a real OSGi framework via bndrun
patterns.description: No mocked framework: test sources become a -tests bundle, resolved and launched by biz.aQute.tester.junit-platform inside Equinox. The bnd resolver computes -runbundles; surefire is disabled entirely.
rules: -tester: biz.aQute.tester.junit-platform
-runrequires: bnd.identity;id='${project.artifactId}-tests' — require the test bundle, resolver pulls the rest
-runbundles is generated by the resolver, never hand-curated (keep -runstartlevel order=sortbynameversion for stable diffs)
Discover test classes via Test-Cases: ${classes;HIERARCHY_INDIRECTLY_ANNOTATED;org.junit.platform.commons.annotation.Testable;CONCRETE} in bnd workspaces
-runfw: org.eclipse.osgi; enable assertions for the library packages via -runvm

patterns.name: Custom AssertJ assertion module per OSGi domain
patterns.description: Each OSGi domain (framework, log, promise, feature) gets its own assertion bundle. Entry-point class per asserted type follows the AssertJ convention: Abstract<Type>Assert holds logic, <Type>Assert is the concrete leaf exposing static assertThat() and an InstanceOfAssertFactory constant for chaining.
rules: Split Abstract<Type>Assert (protected constructor, all assertion methods) from final <Type>Assert (assertThat factory)
Expose public static final InstanceOfAssertFactory<Type, TypeAssert> for asInstanceOf() chains
One bundle per domain keeps consumer dependency surface minimal (Ockham principle)

patterns.name: Example project per consumption mode
patterns.description: examples/ ships the same api+impl+test triple three times: bnd workspace, Gradle, pure Maven. Each is an independently buildable proof that the library works in every mainstream OSGi build setup, CI-verified by a dedicated workflow.
rules: Example test project separated from impl project (org.osgi.test.example.player.test vs .impl)
Test project bnd.bnd: -dependson impl, buildpath uses BSN + workspace macros (${junit}, ${mockito}, ${osgitest})
Keep examples in CI with their own workflow so they fail loudly on API drift
